issues.legal_issue: Proceeds from selling rubber trees held to yield latex and sold after they became unproductive are capital receipts rather than agricultural income.
material_facts: The company owned a rubber estate with trees that were producing latex when acquired.
The company used the trees to obtain income from latex and did not grow them for sale.
After the trees ceased producing latex, the company felled and sold them.
The sale proceeds were included in the computation of agricultural income for tax purposes.
issues.conclusion: The sale proceeds were capital receipts and were not taxable as agricultural income.
issues.legal_principle: Under section 2(a) of the Kerala Agricultural Income-tax Act, 1950, agricultural income is defined by reference to specified income derived from agricultural land and activities; the definition does not include proceeds from selling trees that formed part of the owner's capital assets and had been used to produce income. The court relied on the evidence that the trees were held for latex production and were not grown for sale. No earlier cases are cited.

rule.if: agricultural_income_tax_computation and trees_held_as_producing_assets and trees_not_grown_for_sale and trees_sold_after_latex_yield_ended

predicates.agricultural_income_tax_computation: The dispute arose in a proceeding to determine whether receipts formed agricultural income for tax purposes.
predicates.trees_held_as_producing_assets: The owner held and used the trees as assets for producing latex income.
predicates.trees_not_grown_for_sale: The owner did not grow the trees for the purpose of selling them.
predicates.trees_sold_after_latex_yield_ended: The owner sold the trees after they ceased to produce latex.
predicates.sale_proceeds_are_capital_receipts_not_a: The proceeds from selling the trees are treated as capital receipts and not as agricultural income.

issues.definition: When an agricultural-income tax computation concerns trees held as productive assets, not grown for sale, and sold after their latex yield ends, their sale proceeds are treated as capital receipts rather than agricultural income.
